verdict.rationale: Cua's own docs say Cua Driver lets an agent drive native apps on macOS, Windows and Linux. Separate docs cover connecting Mac, Windows or Linux computers to Spaces, Lume VMs for macOS and Linux, and Windows app build/test workflows, so one agent stack targets several OSes. The community requests for Windows support come from an older early-version thread and are not a concrete hands-on failure of the current claim. Missing for 10: detailed per-target documentation (feature differences, limitations or setup per OS), any mobile target, and independent hands-on corroboration of cross-OS use.

support.subject: As a developer, the same agent targets more than one OS (macOS, Windows, Linux, or mobile) with documented per-target support

citations.quote: Cua Driver: lets an agent drive native apps on macOS, Windows and Linux in the background, through MCP or a CLI.
Connect another Mac, Windows or Linux computer you own to Cua Spaces
Lume: macOS and Linux VMs on Apple silicon.
Your agent builds and tests a Windows app in the background while you keep working.
a hotkey opens a zoomable canvas of live windows from macOS, Linux and Omarchy Spaces
